note: Triennial election of North Down Rural District Council, 1958 (Co. Down county and rural poll day Thursday 5 June 1958). Nominations closed on Tuesday 20 May: the one contest was in Kircubbin, where the retiring member Mr. James Boyd was challenged by Mr. Edward Floyd, a postman; in Kilmood the retiring member was deemed re-elected for want of a nomination; two new members came in for Carrowdore and Crawfordsburn; and thirteen other seats were filled by retiring members (Northern Whig, 21 May 1958, p. 9; Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958, p. 11, which lists the fifteen nominated). Quintin had no member from 1958 until 1964 ('has a representative on North Down Rural Council for the first time in six years', Belfast Telegraph, 20 May 1964, p. 4). No party labels were printed. Returned unopposed (new member).
